steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Mix together croutons and salsa in a large bowl; set aside to soften, about 15 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion, jalapeño pepper, and garlic in hot oil until onion is translucent, 5 to 8 minutes. Remove from heat.

Mix ground chicken, ground pork, pepper Jack cheese, cilantro, egg, taco seasoning, and Worcestershire sauce into crouton mixture; mash any unbroken croutons. Mix into onion mixture in the skillet, then transfer to the prepared loaf pan.
Mix together barbecue sauce and brown sugar in a small bowl, stirring until sugar has dissolved. Brush over meatloaf. Fold a 12-inch-long piece of aluminum foil into a tent and place over meatloaf.

Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 1 hour. Remove the foil tent for the last 10 minutes of baking. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of loaf should read at least 165 degrees F (75 degrees C). Remove meatloaf from the oven, cover with foil, and let stand for 15 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Salsa Chicken Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: This chicken meatloaf with pork is flavored with salsa, taco seasoning, pepper Jack cheese, and seasoned croutons for a zesty south-of-the-border entrée.

review.reviewBody: Amazing....family inhaled this dinner...used whole wheat bread crumbs instead of croutons, a green pepper instead of jalepeno, a full 2 lbs of extra lean ground chicken (used no pork), a whole packet of taco seasoning and a Mexican cheese blend in addition to all of the other ingredients. Very moist and extremely tasty. Loved it!

After reading reviews, I made a few alterations. This review is based on my changes: 1 lb of both chicken and pork, 12 oz salsa, one extra T of taco seasoning. I also used cheddar instead of pepperjack based on personal preference. Didn't put on sauce before putting in oven. Baked uncovered 35 min. Took out, drained, added sauce, baked another 35 minutes. Drained again before serving. It was perfect and delicious! At the table, we sprinkled on a seasoning called Tajin Chili Lime Sauce that took it from great to amazing. Next time I make this, I will add 1 T of the Tajin to the mix, too.

OMG...this was amazing...so moist. Rave reviews from the adults and teens...little ones not so much but they don't like anything but pasta and pizza anyway.... 

I basically followed the recipe although like many others I used 2 lbs of ground chicken and no pork. I used all the other ingredients adjusting the quantities because of the additional meat. I added 4 button mushrooms finely chopped to the onion mixture. I also added about 1/4c bbq sauce to the meat mixture. Once all mixed I felt it was a bit watery so I added about another 1.5 cups of croutons that I quickly ground in the food processor. This seemed the thicken the mixture to the right consistency. With these changes I made 2 loafs. One in a 10 " and one 8". Served the sweet potato fries and roasted broccoli. Can't wait for the left overs tomorrow.

This was awesome and everyone devoured it !
I used 1 lb each ground chicken and pork. Used less salsa and about a cup more of seasoned croutons because I didn’t want it too wet. Also used the entire package of Taco seasoning. 
Did not use loaf pan but free formed it in a 13x9 baking dish lined with foil and baked according to directions . Definitely will be making this again! Loved it!

It's great. Living in Cyprus I had to modify some ingredients. I used 1/2 cup chilli cheese and 1/2 cup parmasen. Also half way through, I drained excess moisture as the previous one I mad was too moist. As for flavor it's excellent and something different in eastern mediteranian. ;)

Like other reviewers, I had a pound of pork and a pound of chicken, so I used both and added more salsa (16oz), taco seasoning (1 pkg) and croutons (maybe two loose cups). I didn't want to have to cook the onion, garlic and spicy pepper bc my hubby doesn't like onions (they are in the salsa anyway) and I didn't have a pepper. Instead, I added four cloves of fresh minced garlic and a can of green chilies directly to the meat. That was way easier and the meatloaf was really delicious and not too spicy for our toddler. The cooking time seemed off for me and I guess I would have had to add another 20 min, but since I didn't have time, I nuked each serving. I took off a star bc 1) my loaf was way too wet, so I would add more croutons in the future and 2) it made a huge mess in my oven! Watch out for that combo of super juicy and BBQ sauce, it drips like mad. I'll bet the leftovers are fantastic and I will be making this again. Thanks for a great spin on traditional meatloaf!

I used a conglomeration of leftovers to add to my new ingredients to make this yummy meatloaf! Half of my salsa was the Trader Joe's tomatillo green salsa and the other half was a red salsa from a local place----both "medium" but really quite hot. My croutons were some of Chef John's from this site that I had in my freezer. Instead of pork I used a Hillshire kielbasa piece that I had in my freezer that I cut into small pieces. I didn't use any jalapeno because of what else I'd used. My taco seasoning was some of what I had on hand (Taco Seasoning I from this site). I did, however, use the instructions and the rest of the ingredients as called for. We calmed down the heat of the salsas with a little sour cream when we ate it, and we LOVED it! It will make either a good leftover meal or great sandwiches for a lunch! Thanks for our dinner! I will definitely make this again!

I used Salsa Verde because it is what I had.
I made little ones instead of one big meatloaf and
will freeze them. I had one last night and it was so good.
I'll be making this again for sure.

Very tasty! I made it close to the original, except I subbed fresh whole wheat bread crumbs for the croutons, used all chicken, and eliminated the jalapeno since my salsa was spicy. I cooked it as patties in a fry pan as another viewer suggested. These were so flavorful they did not need any condiments.

My kiddos (2 and 6) love this as does everyone else who's tried it. I mostly stick to the recipe except for subbing green peppers for the jalapeños and cutting back on taco seasoning and cheese. I've also made this with only turkey, turkey and chicken, only chicken. It's great every time. The possibilities are endless! Leftovers are awesome too. This is one of my favorite Allrecipes finds.

I really didn't know what to expect from a meatloaf using ground chicken and pork, but, wow the taste really packs a punch! It had so much flavor and tasted really fresh using fresh jalapeno and cilantro. My ground chicken and pork came in 1 lb. containers. I noticed that other reviewers used an entire lb. of pork, so, I did to so I didn't have and extra 1/2 lb that I probably wouldn't use. I added a full 2 tbs. of taco seasoning and 16 oz. salsa to accomodate for the extra pork. I left everything else the same. So, so yummy! It was moist and cooked perfectly in the time listed on the recipe. I will definitely be making again. Thanks, HockeyMom!
Love this recipe! Freezes well too.

This was great! I have a go to beef/pork meatloaf recipe that my husband and I both enjoy, but our daughters could take it or leave it. This recipe however, all four of us really enjoyed it. The flavours of the salsa really sung through, and the mildness of the chicken/pork combo worked really well with that. Will make again.

This was amazingly good. I wasn’t sure about it going in. I used 2 pounds ground chicken and no pork. I will mince my onions next time and maybe step up the herbs a little bit not much. Great recipe!!

This was not a win for my family. My husband thought it wasn’t flavorful enough, my kids didn’t like the squishy texture of the stuffing mix (a tip from the reviews), and I really disliked the sauce on top. I followed the recipe exactly and was really disappointed because it sounded like it would please everybody. We eat Mexican a lot and I was expecting more of that type of bold flavor. This was more like bbq, with some taco seasoning mixed in. Just kinda bleh.
this is my favorite meatloaf

Veggie burger instead of pork
Other than that it was delicious!

This was AMAZING!
Make sure you let it sit no less than 15 minutes before eating!!! Let it sit for 20 minutes!
The directions say this by the way!!!
You don't have to drain anything.
In fact, that would be doing yourself a disservice.
Let it cool and harden.
It is moist and delicious.
I just added more seasoning and garlic because I'm a garlic freak, but no changes are needed!!!
It was delicious, moist and savory. Lots of flavor and a lot less fattening than regular meatloaf. My husband and I both love it!

This was a very interesting flavor. Much better than regular meatloaf. We loved it. I made it for my husband and for guests and got rave reviews. Everyone loved it. And any leftovers you might have are even better the next day. Great recipe. Will definitely make again.
